implement: legion-worker: the implementer's rules here — references/pr-body.md (the proof and the PR body; the production-like surfaces reachable in a pod are the pinned Oh My Pi binary and the real MCP server over stdio), references/default-branch-check.md before each push, references/cleanup-deletion.md for the Go cut of packages/daemon/internal/claudebridge/stall.go and its pins, references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md only on a conflict.

ce-simplify-code: the simplify pass over the settled diff. The whole point of this change is that one machine replaces two, so the pass is where the shared module's seam (restore/saveEntry) and the two hosts' adapters are judged as one shape.
dispatch-first: search before any Dispatch write; a problem outside this issue is a dispatch ask, never an issue the implementer files (skill://legion-worker/references/findings.md).
test: legion-worker: references/pr-body.md — the tester drives the application and reads CI for everything static. Here the application is three real surfaces: LEGION_TEST_OMP=/opt/omp/bin/omp bun test extensions/legion-phase-stall-omp.test.ts from packages/pi-legion, bun test from packages/claude-envoy (the real MCP server over stdio against stand-ins), and go test ./... from packages/daemon. The live Claude pane proof (scripts/e2e/claude-backend-tmux.sh) needs a devbox and cannot run in an issue pod; the tester records that rather than claiming it.
dispatch-first: search before any Dispatch write; findings outside this issue are asks.
review: legion-worker: references/review-threads.md for one disposition reply and one resolution per thread, references/merge-gate.md for the order of the round.
ce-simplify-code: the reviewer judges whether the deleted Go copy really left one machine rather than two, and whether the new Claude Code hook endpoint earned its place on the pane's own server.

findings.finding: F1 — the pane's Legion MCP server exposes no tool a hook could call, and spec v26 names neither the tool, its arguments, its answer, nor what happens when the model calls it (envoy-channel-server.ts:1090-1094).
findings.answer: D4: one new tool `legion_phase_hook` beside `legion` and the Envoy tools, taking `{event, …}` and answering one JSON text block (`{}` or `{"decision":"block","reason":…}`). It is visible to the model (measured), so its description says it is Claude Code's hook endpoint, claude-mechanics.md gains a sentence, and a call with a missing or unknown `event` is refused and changes no state.

findings.finding: F2 — the server never sees the daemon's task (bridge.go:402-412 writes it to Claude Code's stdin), yet acceptance 3 requires the count to reset on a task.
findings.answer: D7: a `UserPromptSubmit` mcp_tool hook (measured to fire under Legion's invocation) is the server's sight of every turn start; it classifies the prompt as its own reminder (exact match on the line it last wrote), an Envoy delivery it wrote to the inbox, or a daemon task, and resets the count for the last two.

findings.finding: F3 — a reminder written to the inbox during a turn becomes a step of that turn (bridge.go:430-441,604-630), which would lose the turn boundary the split exists for; the server has no idleness signal.
findings.answer: D9: the timer is armed only at a turn's end (`Stop`, `StopFailure`) or at a resume, and its callback does nothing when a `UserPromptSubmit` has arrived since; the claude-envoy suite drives a timer that fires after a prompt and asserts nothing is written.

findings.finding: F4 — the shared runner's persistence is transcript-shaped (`restore(branch)`, `appendEntry`), which a Claude host has neither of.
findings.answer: D2: `PhaseReminderDeps` grows a persistence seam — `restore(entry)` and `saveEntry(entry)` — so the transcript scan stays in pi-legion and the state file stays in claude-envoy. Recorded as a departure (no acceptance line changes).

findings.finding: F5 — the across-deploy read needs the deployed Go writer's exact path and record (config.go:71, stall.go:92-135), which the spec does not restate.
findings.answer: D5: the same path `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/legion-phase-stall-<session id>.json`, a superset record `{state,count,reported,reportKey}`, written through a temporary file renamed into place before the hook answers, reading `quiet`/`text-call` and a missing count as `{open,0}` through the mapping phase-stall.ts already makes.

findings.finding: F6 — nothing says what a hook answers before the claim boots, in an architect session, or when the record says the phase is over.
findings.answer: D6 and D11: the machine runs only while the claim's role is not `architect`; every hook answers `{}` otherwise, so the bridge's seeding turn is never reminded. The record check is the shared runner's: quiet when the record says the phase is over, fail open on any failure of the read.

findings.finding: F7 — Claude Code may restart the server inside the same claude process, and a plain setTimeout would hold a shut-down server open.
findings.answer: D5 and D9: every count change is written to the file before the hook answers, so a restart loses nothing; the server cancels its pending timer when it arms another and clears them in `stop()`.

findings.finding: F8 — the architect's instruction puts the hooks in the shared `packages/claude-envoy/hooks/hooks.json`, which is also loaded outside Legion where no `legion` MCP server exists.
findings.answer: D3 puts them in the generated Legion-only plugin `packages/claude-envoy/legion/hooks/hooks.json`, which a pane loads as a second --plugin-dir (claude.go:106-108). Recorded as a departure from the architect's instruction; one file move reverses it.

findings.finding: F9 — a Legion pane might run two servers from this package (the pane's `legion` and the plugin's own `envoy`), and the hook names one.
findings.answer: Measured (M7): with `--strict-mcp-config` the plugin's own `.mcp.json` server does not appear; the session's `mcp_servers` held only the one `--mcp-config` registers. No further work.

findings.finding: F10 — `/clear` mints a new session id and would orphan a state file keyed by the old one.
findings.answer: D5 declares `/clear` out of scope: a Legion pane runs `claude -p` with a `--session-id`/`--resume` the daemon names, and no worker runs it. The file keys on the Claude Code session id, as the deployed Go file does.

findings.finding: F11 — what the `Stop` hook returns on the second Stop of a run, what an error answer costs, and whether the record check runs inside the hook.
findings.answer: D8 and D11: the block is used only when the count is 0; a later `Stop` answers `{}` and arms the timer. The record check runs inside the `Stop` hook, bounded at 5 s, with the hook's own timeout declared 30 s; a failed read fails open.

findings.finding: F12 — the Go deletion set is larger than the spec's three nouns and includes symbols that exist only to feed the machine.
findings.answer: D12 lists every one: stall.go whole; the bridge's `stall`, `lastAssistantText`, `handoffs`, their initialisation, both `setStall` calls, the `step` reset, the `assistant` accumulation, `isLegionTool`, `toolResults` and its `case "user"` caller, the settle branch and `setStall`; `Config.StallFile` and the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` refusal that exists only for it; and each named test, helper and surviving `FollowUp` use in bridge_test.go.

findings.finding: F13 — two live-proof scripts and the e2e README encode the old one-follow-up behaviour and parse the transcript entry.
findings.answer: T9: their prose changes; their predicates do not, because the entry keeps its `customType` and its `state` field and both assert only that no follow-up comes after a successful completion, which a closed phase still satisfies. Neither can be run from an issue pod, which the plan says.

findings.finding: F14 — the move needs three new `exports` entries and a self-reference fix, and pi-legion's tsconfig wildcard would hide a missing entry until claude-envoy's bundle fails.
findings.answer: D1 names the three entries, the rewrite of phase-stall.ts's first import to `./interface`, the relative sibling imports, and `bun run typecheck` in packages/claude-envoy as the check that catches a missing entry.

findings.finding: F15 — claude-envoy type-checks imported sources under stricter flags than pi-shared's.
findings.answer: D1 requires `bunx tsc --noEmit` in all three packages and keeps the moved files on pi-shared's own biome recipe.

findings.finding: F16 — two committed generated trees (`dist/`, `legion/`) are pinned byte for byte to a fresh build on the pinned Bun.
findings.answer: T2 requires `bun run build` and the commit of both, with `bun run check-dist` as the check; the pod's Bun is 1.3.14, which is `.bun-version` (measured), so the build runs here.

findings.finding: F17 — `tests/hooks-timeout.test.ts` assumes every hook is a command hook with `args` and pins exactly three rows.
findings.answer: T8 rewrites it to cover both hook kinds and both files, with the five mcp_tool timeouts D3 names.

findings.finding: F18 — the shared module's comments say `reported`/`reportKey` are the Oh My Pi plugin's alone, while acceptance 9 requires the architect notice and its retry on Claude Code.
findings.answer: D11: both fields ride the Claude state file, and the two comments are corrected with the move.

findings.finding: F19 — the four variables have no acceptance criterion, and `spec.Env` is replaced wholesale by the git identity's map, so anything added before that line is lost.
findings.answer: D13: `workerSpawnSpec` copies the four from the daemon's own environment into `spec.Env` after that line; both runtimes already forward `spec.Env`. The plan adds the missing acceptance criterion (§3, line 12) and three Go tests.

findings.finding: F20 — four acceptance bullets cannot be decided in an issue pod, one of them only on a devbox, and the Claude e2e has no step today in which a worker ends a turn with its phase open.
findings.answer: §3 maps every bullet to a suite and a command and marks the live-pane line devbox-only; T3 adds the missing e2e step before the script's successful handoff_complete step and makes reporting the devbox need to the architect part of the work.

findings.finding: F21 — three documents beyond the three the spec names state the behaviour being removed.
findings.answer: T9 lists them all: docs/deployment.md:198-202, packages/claude-envoy/AGENTS.md (a new section), workflow/review.go:431-435, the e2e README and the two script headers, both CHANGELOGs, the worker skill and headless.md.

findings.finding: F22 — four named risks: the cosmetic stop-hook-error, the model-visible hook tool, a PostToolUse round-trip per tool call, and a deployed Claude Code older than the measured build.
findings.answer: §4 risks 1 and 3–5 accept and name each, with the live-pane proof as the only thing that settles the version question.

findings.finding: F23 — five claims about Claude Code that the repository cannot establish (PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure firing, StopFailure, a helper agent's id, and the hook arming).
findings.answer: Four of the five were measured in this pod on Claude Code 2.1.310 and are recorded as M1–M7 in the plan; `StopFailure` and a subagent's `agent_id` remain unmeasured and are §4 risks 2 and 7, with the live-pane proof as where they show.

findings.finding: F24 — acceptance 1's "the first reminder" reads either as the first of a run or the first of the stall, and the two give different reminder counts on Claude Code.
findings.answer: D8 reads it as the first of the stall, keyed on the count being 0 exactly as the Oh My Pi half already is; recorded as a departure, since the acceptance test counts reminders.

specDepartures.spec: "the Legion plugin already ships hooks that Claude Code finds by itself (packages/claude-envoy/hooks/hooks.json), so the reminder needs no new flag and no new process: the hooks are entries in that file" — and the architect's instruction repeating it.
specDepartures.plan: The five hook entries are generated into the Legion-only plugin packages/claude-envoy/legion/hooks/hooks.json, which a Legion pane loads as its second --plugin-dir; the shared hooks/hooks.json is left as it is.
specDepartures.evidence: A Legion pane loads both directories (packages/daemon/internal/runtime/tmux/claude.go:106-108), while @sjawhar/claude-envoy is installed as a plain Claude Code plugin elsewhere and ships hooks/** to every installer (package.json files list); outside a pane no `legion` MCP server exists, and Claude Code answers an mcp_tool hook whose server is not connected with a non-blocking hook error on every turn (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, "When the server is still connecting"). The cost of the change is one generated file in buildLegionPlugin, pinned by tests/legion-plugin-fresh.test.ts; one file move reverses it.

settledDecisions.decision: The new hooks are entries in packages/claude-envoy/hooks/hooks.json.
settledDecisions.detail: They are entries in the generated Legion-only plugin instead, so a non-Legion Claude Code session that loads this package never fires a hook against a server it does not have.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 1: "the first reminder as the end-of-turn hook's own continuation, every later one as a turn started for it", with the Claude Code prose "The first reminder of a run is the `Stop` hook's block".
specDepartures.plan: The block is the first reminder of the stall, not of each run: the `Stop` hook blocks only while the count is 0, so a reminder that arrived over the inbox does not earn a second block when its own run ends.
specDepartures.evidence: Measured in this pod on Claude Code 2.1.310: a blocked Stop continues the turn and the next Stop carries stop_hook_active: true, so only within one run is a block distinguishable; every inbox reminder starts a run of its own, whose Stop would otherwise block again, giving two reminders per cycle and a count that climbs twice. The Oh My Pi half already keys the continuation on count === 0 (packages/pi-legion/src/phase-reminder.ts:329-342), and the acceptance test counts reminders.

acceptance: "the first reminder as the end-of-turn hook's own continuation" -> the first reminder of each stall is the end-of-turn hook's continuation (the Stop hook's block on Claude Code); every later reminder, including the one that ends the run a reminder started, is a turn started for the worker.

specDepartures.spec: "passing them to a worker that way is part of this work, since the daemon passes a pane and a pod only the variables it names" — stated in the prose with no acceptance bullet.
specDepartures.plan: The plan adds a twelfth acceptance criterion: a pane's -e pairs and a pod container's env carry each of the four LEGION_STALL_* variables the daemon's own environment holds, decided by Go tests in packages/daemon.
specDepartures.evidence: No acceptance bullet of spec v26 mentions the variables; the seam is spec.Env (packages/daemon/internal/daemon/specs.go:125-166, forwarded at runtime/tmux/spawn.go:205-211 and runtime/sandbox/manifest.go:932-935), and spec.Env is replaced wholesale by the git identity's map at specs.go:160, so an implementer could satisfy the prose and leave nothing proven.

acceptance: added: a pane's -e pairs and a pod container's env carry each of LEGION_STALL_REMINDER_MS, LEGION_STALL_WAITING_MS, LEGION_STALL_RESUME_MS and LEGION_STALL_ARCHITECT_AFTER that the daemon holds, proven by go test ./... in packages/daemon.

specDepartures.spec: "packages/pi-legion/src/phase-stall.ts, phase-reminder.ts and stall-limits.ts move into @legion/pi-shared, where the Oh My Pi plugin and the pane's Legion server both import them."
specDepartures.plan: They move as the spec says, and the runner's persistence changes shape with the move: restore(branch) becomes restore(entry) and appendEntry becomes saveEntry, so each host supplies its own storage (the Oh My Pi transcript, the Claude Code state file).
specDepartures.evidence: packages/pi-legion/src/phase-reminder.ts:53-60,300-308 reads and writes an Oh My Pi transcript branch through pi.appendEntry and restorePhaseStall; a Claude Code host has neither, and the alternative — fabricating a one-entry branch in the server — would put a fake transcript entry in a program that has no transcript.
